interpretations: Average postseason doubles per record is computed per player (each player_id with one batting hand), as the mean of the `double` column over that player's batting_postseason rows, ignoring NULL values. The overall average is the mean of these per-player averages, with each player counted equally.
The overall average is the mean of the per-player averages taken across all players with a non-empty, non-NULL batting hand. The index is the player's average divided by this value.
The overall average is instead the average of all postseason doubles records pooled together, ignoring NULLs. Under this reading the denominator is not an average of per-player averages.
The hand average is the mean of the players' index values, with each player counted equally, over players with the same `bats` value. The difference is the player's index minus this mean.
The hand average is computed as a record-weighted average of the index within each batting hand, rather than a player-weighted one.
The grouping is by player and batting hand, so one row per (player_id, bats) pair. Each player has one batting hand, so this gives one row per player.
Players with no batting_postseason records are excluded because they have no average. Alternatively, they are included with a NULL average, and the NULL ends up last in the sort.

Players whose postseason `double` values are all NULL get a NULL average. These are either excluded from the overall average and the hand average, or kept in the output with NULL index and NULL difference, sorted last.

Players with `bats` NULL or the empty string '' are excluded entirely, both from the output and from the overall average. Alternatively, only NULL is treated as missing, and the empty string counts as its own hand group.
The batting hand values are R, L and B (switch hitters). B is treated as its own hand group. Alternatively, B is merged with another group.
The output is the top 10 players by difference, sorted from highest to lowest, with NULLs last. Ties at the 10th position are broken arbitrarily, or all tied players are included.
The output columns are player_id, bats, average doubles, index, and index minus hand average. No rounding is applied.
"Furthest above" means the largest positive difference (index minus hand average) in descending order. Alternatively, it means the largest absolute difference, in either direction.
The join between batting_postseason and player on `player_id` is an inner join. Alternatively, it is a left join from player, which keeps players with no postseason records.
Missing interpretations:
The per-player average is taken per postseason record, so each batting_postseason row counts once. Rows with NULL `double` are dropped from the count, not treated as 0.
Missing `double` values are instead treated as 0, so they count as records in the denominator.
The hand average is the mean of the index over the same-hand players, and it includes the player being compared.
The hand average excludes the player being compared (leave-one-out).
The hand average is taken over all players with that `bats` value in the player table, not only those with postseason records.
The hand average is the average of the players' raw average doubles divided by the overall average, which is equivalent to the mean of the indexes.
The overall average is computed over the per-(player, bats) groups after the NULL and empty-`bats` filter, and this filter is applied before any aggregation.
A zero overall average would make the index undefined (NULL or an error).
The sort is by the difference only, and ties are broken by player_id or left unspecified.
"Unrounded" means the full floating-point precision is returned, with no casting to integer. Integer division is avoided because `double` is stored as an integer in this table.
Whitespace-only `bats` values are also treated as empty.
queries:
SELECT AVG(player_avg) 
FROM (
    SELECT bp.player_id, AVG(bp."double") AS player_avg
    FROM batting_postseason bp
    JOIN player p ON p.player_id = bp.player_id
    WHERE p.bats IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY bp.player_id
);
SELECT player_id
FROM batting_postseason
GROUP BY player_id
HAVING AVG(double) > (SELECT AVG(double) FROM batting_postseason);
SELECT player_id,
       <index_expr> - AVG(<index_expr>) OVER (PARTITION BY bats) AS difference
FROM player
WHERE <index_expr> IS NOT NULL AND bats IS NOT NULL;
SELECT p.bats, AVG(p.weight * 703.0 / (p.height * p.height)) AS avg_bmi
FROM batting b
JOIN player p ON b.player_id = p.player_id
WHERE p.bats IS NOT NULL AND p.height > 0 AND p.weight > 0
GROUP BY p.bats;
